desc:
Given a binary search tree with distinct values and an integer x, find

  • the floor of x: the largest value in the tree that is ≤ x, and
  • the ceiling of x: the smallest value in the tree that is ≥ x.

Return them as [floor, ceiling]. If one of them does not exist, write -1 in its place. If x is in the tree, both are equal to x.

Tree encoding. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order. The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn, level by level, from left to right. A missing child is written as -1 (node values are never negative, so -1 cannot be confused with a value). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped. The empty tree is [].

For example, [8,3,10,1,6,-1,14] is the tree whose root 8 has children 3 and 10; node 3 has children 1 and 6; node 10 has no left child and right child 14.

Example 1

tree = [8,3,10,1,6,-1,14,-1,-1,4,7,13], x = 5
Output: [4,6]

Example 2

tree = [8,3,10,1,6,-1,14,-1,-1,4,7,13], x = 0
Output: [-1,1]
No value is ≤ 0.

Example 3

tree = [8,3,10,1,6,-1,14,-1,-1,4,7,13], x = 20
Output: [14,-1]
constraints: 0 ≤ node value ≤ 100,000, all values distinct; the tree is a valid BST
hints: The inorder sequence of a BST is sorted, so the floor and the ceiling are the neighbours of x in that sorted order. Can you find them without visiting every node?
Walk down from the root as in a normal search. When the current value is smaller than x it is a floor candidate, and anything better can only be in its right subtree.
Keep two variables, floor and ceil, both starting at -1. Value < x: floor = value, go right. Value > x: ceil = value, go left. Value == x: both are x. Stop at a missing child.
editorial: Search for x from the root and remember the best candidates seen on the way. When the current value is smaller than x, it is a valid floor, and every better floor must be larger than it, hence in the right subtree: record it and go right. When the current value is larger, it is a valid ceiling and a better one can only be on the left: record it and go left. An exact match settles both answers at once.
Every step is a plain BST search step, so the walk follows one root-to-leaf path: O(h) after the O(n) decoding of the array. Because values are never negative, -1 is a safe 'does not exist' marker.
